title: When the Horizon Burns Anew
premise: Orsen Whitlock, a clone who inherited the original's unsolved murder case, has spent six years documenting the slow collapse of the colony at Meridian's Edge while the fleet above maintains a fragile truce. When a ship that never flew appears on the registry with an unfamiliar name aboard — Sera Voss — Orsen discovers she is the courier of a message that could end the war between the fleet and the colonists, or ignite it before the truce expires. Together they uncover that the original Whitlock was murdered because he found the message first, and that the colony's death was engineered to bury it. In the end, Orsen must choose between preserving his inherited identity and broadcasting the truth under his own name, ending the war but erasing the man he was cloned to replace.
about_author: Wendell Almeida is a former orbital logistics analyst who spent a decade writing technical postmortems for failed off-world ventures before turning to fiction. He lives in Lisbon, where he writes about people who inherit other people's consequences.

chapters.title: The Inheritance Clause
chapters.summary: POV: Orsen. Orsen wakes in the cloning vat with the original's memories up to the moment of his murder, legally bound to finish the dead man's case. He walks through Meridian's Edge, cataloguing its decay for his records. Emotional beat: disorientation and quiet grief for a life that isn't quite his.

chapters.title: Manifest of a Ghost
chapters.summary: POV: Orsen. Auditing old fleet manifests, Orsen finds the freighter Calyx listed as arriving — a ship destroyed before it ever launched, carrying one passenger name he doesn't recognize: Sera Voss. The record updates itself while he watches. Emotional beat: creeping dread that the case is still active.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Wasn't There
chapters.summary: POV: Sera. Sera Voss comes out of cryostasis on a ship she was told never flew, crewed by strangers who call her 'the courier' and refuse to answer questions. She memorizes exits. Emotional beat: controlled fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Six Years of Rain
chapters.summary: POV: Orsen. Orsen reviews his predecessor's murder file: three suspects, all dead or vanished, and a sealed evidence chip the fleet courts refuse to unseal. A colonist warns him someone from orbit has been asking about him. Emotional beat: the loneliness of being both detective and victim.

chapters.title: Descent Vector
chapters.summary: POV: Sera. The Calyx makes an unauthorized descent to Meridian's Edge; the crew reveals Sera's message must be delivered before the fleet's truce expires in nineteen days. She escapes during landing chaos and vanishes into the colony. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into self-reliance.

chapters.title: Two Names, One Face
chapters.summary: POV: Orsen. Orsen intercepts Sera in the hydroponics levels; she mistakes him for the original Whitlock and attacks him. They reach an armed standoff, then a wary bargain: she needs someone who knows the colony, he needs her manifest connection. Emotional beat: mutual suspicion becoming reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: What the Colony Remembers
chapters.summary: POV: Orsen. Following the original's notes, they visit witnesses who describe a fleet operation years ago that poisoned the water grid — the engineered decline Orsen has been documenting. Someone burns down the archive behind them. Emotional beat: horror at realizing the death he recorded was deliberate.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days
chapters.summary: POV: Sera. Sera admits the message is encoded in her own memory, keyed to unlock only at the original Whitlock's terminal — which is why he was murdered. The truce clock becomes explicit. Emotional beat: the weight of being a weapon disguised as a person.

chapters.title: The Terminal Problem
chapters.summary: POV: Orsen. The original's terminal sits inside the sealed judicial annex, guarded by fleet marshals who answer to the very faction that killed him. Orsen plans the infiltration using his legal inheritance rights as cover. Emotional beat: cold clarity, the detective finally working the case.

chapters.title: Truce Line
chapters.summary: POV: Sera. Fleet warships begin repositioning overhead; colonists riot at the spaceport. Sera sees news feeds branding her a terrorist courier and realizes both sides want her dead once delivered. Emotional beat: isolation — no faction is hers.

chapters.title: The Marshal's Offer
chapters.summary: POV: Orsen. Marshal Idris Kane, the original's prime suspect, corners Orsen and offers immunity: hand over the courier, and the case closes clean. Orsen stalls, buying time, and notices Kane wears the original's missing evidence chip as a trophy. Emotional beat: temptation and revulsion in equal measure.

chapters.title: Waterline
chapters.summary: POV: Sera. Hiding in the flooded lower tiers, Sera decrypts fragments of her own memory and glimpses the message: proof the fleet command ordered the colony's poisoning to justify martial consolidation. Emotional beat: grief for the person she was before she became a vessel.

chapters.title: Inheritance Rights
chapters.summary: POV: Orsen. Orsen invokes his clone-inheritance status to enter the annex legally, walking past the guards as 'Whitlock.' Inside, he finds the original's final log: a warning that any clone completing the case would be terminated too. Emotional beat: understanding his own expiration date.

chapters.title: Kane's Net
chapters.summary: POV: Sera. Kane's marshals raid the lower tiers; Sera is captured but transmits her location to Orsen first. Kane interrogates her gently, almost kindly, revealing he believes delivering the message will start the war — and he wants it to. Emotional beat: the horror of a true believer.

chapters.title: Four Days
chapters.summary: POV: Orsen. With four days left, Orsen assembles the colony's survivors — the people he documented dying — into an unlikely escort. His records become their map of safe routes. Emotional beat: purpose; the documentation was preparation all along.

chapters.title: The Annex Breach
chapters.summary: POV: alternating. The assault on the judicial annex goes wrong; two colonists die covering Orsen's approach to the terminal. He reaches it as alarms seal the building. Emotional beat: sacrifice made concrete, guilt carried forward.

chapters.title: Unlock
chapters.summary: POV: Orsen. At the terminal, the message requires both the original's credentials and the courier's presence — Kane arrives with Sera, intending to control the delivery. Orsen triggers the unlock; the full truth floods every colony screen. Emotional beat: triumph immediately shadowed by consequence.

chapters.title: What the Message Says
chapters.summary: POV: Sera. The broadcast exposes the poisoning order — and a second clause: the fleet council voted unanimously, meaning there is no clean faction to surrender to. Fleet crews begin defecting to the surface. Kane, exposed, tries to destroy the terminal and Sera with it. Emotional beat: vertigo — victory and apocalypse in one breath.

chapters.title: The Burning Horizon
chapters.summary: POV: alternating. Kane's sabotage ignites the annex; Orsen chooses to stay and hold the manual override so the broadcast completes, telling Sera the message needed a sender with skin in it. She escapes as the horizon glows with burning ships and burning archives. Emotional beat: Orsen's acceptance — the clone dies as himself, not as the original.

chapters.title: After the Signal
chapters.summary: POV: Sera. The truce collapses into scattered skirmishes, then halts as defections paralyze fleet command. Sera, carrying Orsen's final records, addresses the assembled colonists and defected crews. Emotional beat: exhausted responsibility — the courier becomes a witness.

chapters.title: The Second Clone
chapters.summary: POV: Sera. Fleet remnants offer terms; part of them includes a new Whitlock clone grown from backup tissue, inheriting nothing but the name. Sera must decide whether to tell him what he was made to forget. Emotional beat: mercy versus protection, the ethics of inheritance.

chapters.title: When the Horizon Burns Anew
chapters.summary: POV: Sera. Months later, the colony rebuilds on documented truth rather than myth. Sera gives the new clone Orsen's records and lets him choose whether to read them, then walks out to watch dawn break over repaired solar arrays. Emotional beat: hard-won hope — survival paid for, and worth it.
